title: Ben Horowitz on Raising a New Fund and How Venture Firms Scale

reader_summary.headline: Ben Horowitz explains how venture firms scale and help founders build great companies.
reader_summary.overview: Ben Horowitz argues that venture capital must offer founders networks and advice, not just money. He explains how his firm manages conflicts and scales by focusing on finding truth rather than just winning deals. The discussion covers why large teams struggle and how platforms help startups succeed.

key_points.text: Venture capital should provide founders with a strong network and practical advice, not just money.
key_points.evidence_quote: a much better product would be, give me, like, the network to be confident and the advice I need to run this fucking thing.

key_points.text: The firm prioritizes helping entrepreneurs build strong companies over simply beating stock market returns.
key_points.evidence_quote: our mission isn't to get higher returns than the S&P 500, although that's a good side effect or whatever. You know, our mission is much more to like, can we help the best entrepreneurs build the best companies

key_points.text: Large venture firms fail when shared control creates chaos or when too many people make it hard to find the truth.
key_points.evidence_quote: if you have shared control, you just can't get past a certain size before it becomes some chaotic, crazy democracy

notes: In this feed drop from Uncapped , Jack Altman sits down with a16z co-founder Ben Horowitz to unpack the founding bet behind Andreessen Horowitz. VC should be a better product for entrepreneurs, built on real operating experience, real networks, and real support. Ben shares how he and Marc Andreessen have worked together for 30 years, how they make decisions, and what it takes to scale a venture firm without losing the edge that actually helps founders. They also dig into why boards matter, how platform teams can change what partners do day-to-day, and the difference between “heat-seeking” investing and conviction-driven company building, especially in sectors like AI and crypto.
